Naming a child after a star is believed to bring the blessings and protection of that celestial body.

historical_references.reference: Qandil was a fortress city in the Armenian Highlands during the Seljuk Empire. It was an important strategic point for the control of the Silk Road trade routes.
historical_references.context: The Seljuk Empire was a Turkish empire that emerged in the 11th century CE and controlled a large area of the Middle East. Qandil was an important city in this empire and was strategically located along the Silk Road trade routes, making it a valuable asset for control of commerce and power.

historical_references.reference: Qandil is also the name of a mountain range in northern Iraq, which has been a significant site of conflict between various groups, including the Kurdish militant group the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK).
historical_references.context: The Qandil mountains have been a site of conflict between various groups, most notably the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK) and the Iraqi and Turkish governments. The PKK has used the mountains as a base of operations and has launched attacks against both countries from this location.
